title: granite-bay-retail-integration-call-notes-2026-07-29
content:
Meeting: Granite Bay Retail — integration kickoff (payments risk/merchant matching)
Date: 2026-07-29
Attendees: Ethan Brooks (Granite Bay — Eng), Lina Ortiz (Granite Bay — PM), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood Solutions), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SRE)

High-level ask/goal:
- Short term: integrate Redwood API to run merchant fraud scoring + product matching for chargeback investigation workflows.
- Long term: migrate some latency-sensitive inference to Dedicated capacity (SLA) and evaluate Private (VPC) for PCI scope reduction.

Customer background:
- Mid-market retail chain, handles ~1200 txn/sec peak across POS + e-commerce.
- Currently using an in-house rules engine + 3rd-party fraud API; want ML to reduce manual review while keeping false positives low.
- PCI requirements: cardholder data cannot be stored in third-party logs; they want guidance on minimizing scope.

Technical requirements / constraints:
- Target latency: p95 end-to-end for fraud score API <= 200ms for online checkout (they consider up to 300ms acceptable for non-critical async flows).
- Throughput: steady 400 rps with spikes to 1200 rps (holiday peaks).
- Input size: typical request ~120 tokens (transaction + merchant metadata + sparse user history), some batched investigations up to 1k tokens.
- Output: structured JSON with score + explanation tokens (max ~60 tokens).
- Security: TLS 1.3, client mTLS for Dedicated/private plan, KMS integration for any stored keys.
- Data retention: no raw PANs in logs. They will tokenize/mask card data client-side; still want advice on redaction and telemetry.

Integration approach discussed:
- Phase 1 (quick PoC): hosted Redwood API from region us-west-2, sync calls for real-time checkout scoring. Use masking on client side and send tokenized card id only.
- Phase 2: evaluate Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable latency at peak. Add autoscaling policy for holiday bursts and a fallback route to a cheaper / lower-capacity model if Dedicated saturated.
- Phase 3: Private deployment if PCI auditors require out-of-band control plane + VPC connectivity.

Architectural notes + recommendations (Ravi/Maya):
- Use continuous batching with low max-batch-wait (<= 5ms) to meet latency SLO for checkout. Configure smaller batch sizes for checkout route and larger for investigations route.
- Enable prefix/KV cache for frequent merchant metadata and static product embeddings to reduce token compute. Precompute merchant embeddings for top-10k merchants and store in cache (evict policy LRU).
- Model selection: start with mid-sized model (e.g., 7B quantized) for cost/latency balance. Provide path to switch to a lower-latency Llama-variant on Dedicated if needed.
- Response formatting: use strict JSON schema + function-call style responses to simplify downstream parsing and prevent hallucinated fields.

Gotchas / unresolved items (need follow-up):
- PCI scope & logs: they want assurance that hosted logs won't store masked PANs and want an option to disable request/response logging for checkout route. Need to confirm whether hosted API can accept a no-logs profile or only Dedicated/Private can guarantee zero logging. (Action: confirm with product/infra)
- Idempotency for retries: their retry gateway currently retries on 502s without idempotency keys. We recommended idempotency keys per txn id; need engineering to confirm how Redwood SDK supports idempotency metadata and partial retries.
- Billing/metric attribution: they want per-route token cost/latency breakdown for chargeback investigations to allocate to Ops vs Fraud teams. Confirm tagging options and per-route reporting retention.
- Mutual TLS for Dedicated: customer wants mTLS for Dedicated endpoints. Confirm cert management workflow and whether we can support ACME-style rotation or require manual upload.
- Model explainability: they want short textual explanations with each score. Need guardrails to avoid leaking PII in explanations; propose templated rationale + pointer to feature IDs rather than raw data.

Risk/mitigation notes:
- Risk: Hosted API may expand PCI scope if auditors are strict. Mitigation: propose Dedicated + single-tenant logs + limited retention; negotiate a short-term exception for PoC with tokenization and no logging enabled on checkout route.
- Risk: spikes could saturate batchers causing latency cliffs. Mitigation: route checkout traffic to a low-latency pool with priority preemption and configure circuit-breakers/backpressure to fallback to simpler rule-based score if necessary.

Action items / next steps:
- Maya: open SE-4321 in Jira capturing PCI/logging questions and idempotency support. (Due: 2026-08-03)
- Ravi: prototype PoC request shape + sample code (Node + Python) for tokenization + API call. Share in Github PR template. (Due: 2026-08-05)
- Sofia: validate mTLS workflow with infra team and document cert rotation options; confirm if auto-rotation supported. (Due: 2026-08-06)
- Ethan/Lina (customer): provide sample anonymized payloads (1 week) and expected QPS profile by route (checkout vs investigations).
- Maya: schedule follow-up technical deep-dive with infra and product to discuss logging controls and Dedicated SLA options. (Propose 2026-08-07)

Notes to self / SE tips for PoC:
- For PoC, use streaming disabled for checkout (simpler) and enable structured function-calling for investigations to get JSON output.
- Keep max_tokens low and use stop tokens to avoid long explanations.
- Add a layer of client-side redaction: mask PAN segments and remove CVV before sending. Keep a hashed txn id for idempotency.
- Add request headers: X-Client-Txn, X-Route (checkout|investigation), X-Feature-Flags for per-route config.

References/links:
- Confluence draft: RB-Integrations/Granite-Bay-Retail-PCI-Notes
- Jira: SE-4321 (placeholder; will link once created)
- Example SDK snippet PR: github.com/redwood-inference/integration-samples/pull/84

Informal: customer seemed anxious about auditors — emphasize Dedicated/private as an option but get PoC running fast so they can show progress. Keep follow-up focused on concrete deliverables (payloads, QPS, cert questions).
